grammarName.en: used to · would · be/get used to
grammarName.ru: used to · would · be/get used to

scenario: Peter finds an old photo of the office, and the team reminisces about how things used to be — so the episode is full of 'used to', 'would' for repeated past actions, and 'be/get used to' for habits. Kate: 'We used to have just one computer, and we all shared it.' Den: 'I would always arrive first and make the coffee.' Alex: 'The office used to be tiny. There didn't use to be a plant.' Pol: 'Valery would grumble every single morning — I miss it now that he has retired.' Peter says, 'I'm still getting used to the new coffee machine.' Kate: 'We're all used to working together now.' Warm nostalgia, gentle humour, a soft callback to Valery's retirement. Use clear contrasts: 'used to + verb' (past state/habit that stopped), 'would + verb' (repeated past action), and 'be/get used to + -ing' (being accustomed). Short B1 sentences.
